66222-mrs-siddons.creator: Mrs. A. Kennard.
66222-mrs-siddons.description: A book by Mrs. A. Kennard.. n passed entirely before the public, it is necessary to divest the character as much as possible of the legendary traditions adhering to it. It must be brought down into the regions of ordinary life, and the only way to accomplish this is to transcribe her actual words and expressions written without thought of publication.

9220-the-threefold-destiny-from-twice-to.title: The Threefold Destiny From Twice Told Tales
9220-the-threefold-destiny-from-twice-to.creator: Unknown
9220-the-threefold-destiny-from-twice-to.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. rer again trod the street of his native village, it is no wonder that he passed unrecognized, though exciting the gaze and curiosity of all. Yet, as his arm casually touched that of a young woman, who was wending her way to an evening lecture, she started, and almost uttered a cry.

arxiv-1905-04492.title: Structural Equation Models as Computation Graphs
arxiv-1905-04492.creator: Erik-Jan van Kesteren, Daniel Oberski
arxiv-1905-04492.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Erik-Jan van Kesteren, Daniel Oberski. Structural equation modeling (SEM) is a popular tool in the social and behavioural sciences, where it is being applied to ever more complex data types. The high-dimensional data produced by modern sensors, brain images, or (epi)genetic measurements require variable selection using parameter penalization; experimental models combining disparate data sources benefit from regularization to obtain a stable result; and genomic SEM or network models lead to alternative objective functions.

arxiv-2010-03600.title: Detecting Anomalous Graphs in Labeled Multi-Graph Databases CCS: Information systems Data mining CCS: Computing methodologies Anomaly detection
arxiv-2010-03600.creator: Hung T. Nguyen, Pierre J. Liang, Leman Akoglu
arxiv-2010-03600.description: Abstract . Within a large database 𝒢 \mathcal{G} containing graphs with labeled nodes and directed, multi-edges; how can we detect the anomalous graphs? Most existing work are designed for plain (unlabeled) and/or simple (unweighted) graphs. We introduce CODEtect , the first approach that addresses the anomaly detection task for graph databases with such complex nature.

arxiv-2104-14314.title: MOROCCO: Model Resource Comparison Framework CCS: Computing methodologies Model verification and validation CCS: Computing methodologies Natural language processing CCS: Information systems Document representation
arxiv-2104-14314.creator: Valentin Malykh, Ekaterina Artemova, Alexander Kukushkin, Tatiana Shavrina, Vladislav Mikhailov, Maria Tikhonova
arxiv-2104-14314.description: Abstract . The new generation of pre-trained NLP models push the SOTA to the new limits, but at the cost of computational resources, to the point that their use in real production environments is often prohibitively expensive. We tackle this problem by evaluating not only the standard quality metrics on downstream tasks but also the memory footprint and inference time.

arxiv-2207-10354.title: Learning from Data with Noisy Labels Using Temporal Self-Ensemble
arxiv-2207-10354.creator: Jun Ho Lee, Jae Soon Baik, Tae Hwan Hwang, and Jun Won Choi
arxiv-2207-10354.description: Abstract There are inevitably many mislabeled data in real-world datasets. Because deep neural networks (DNNs) have an enormous capacity to memorize noisy labels, a robust training scheme is required to prevent labeling errors from degrading the generalization performance of DNNs. Current state-of-the-art methods present a co-training scheme that trains dual networks using samples associated with small losses.

arxiv-2209-13069.title: Signs of environmental effects on star-forming galaxies in the Spiderweb protocluster at z=2.16 2022 Signs of environmental effects on star-forming galaxies in the Spiderweb protocluster at z=2.16 – 3
arxiv-2209-13069.creator: J. M. Pérez-Martínez, H. Dannerbauer, T. Kodama, Y. Koyama, R. Shimakawa, T. L. Suzuki, R. Calvi, Z. Chen, K. Daikuhara, N. A. Hatch, A. Laza-Ramos, D. Sobral, J. P. Stott, I. Tanaka
arxiv-2209-13069.description: Abstract We use multi-object near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy with VLT/KMOS to investigate the role of the environment in the evolution of the ionized gas properties of narrow-band selected H α \alpha emitters (HAEs) in the Spiderweb protocluster at z = 2.16 z=2.16 .

arxiv-2311-04081.title: Learning Super-Resolution Ultrasound Localization Microscopy from Radio-Frequency Data Thanks: This work is funded by the Hasler Foundation under project number 22027. ⋆ Corresponding author email: christopher.hahne [ät] unibe.ch
arxiv-2311-04081.creator: Christopher Hahne ⋆ \star, Georges Chabouh, Olivier Couture, Raphael Sznitman
arxiv-2311-04081.description: Abstract Ultrasound Localization Microscopy (ULM) enables imaging of vascular structures in the micrometer range by accumulating contrast agent particle locations over time. Precise and efficient target localization accuracy remains an active research topic in the ULM field to further push the boundaries of this promising medical imaging technology.

arxiv-2311-17931.title: Model Theory of Ultrafinitism II: Deconstructing the Term Model (First Draft)
arxiv-2311-17931.creator: Mirco A. Mannucci
arxiv-2311-17931.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Mirco A. Mannucci. This paper presents a novel possible worlds semantics, designed to elucidate the underpinnings of ultrafinitism. By constructing a careful modification of the well-known Kripke models for inuitionistic logic, we seek to extend our comprehension of the ultra-finite mindset. As it turns out, the passage from standard constructivist mathematics to the ultrafinite is in a sense an operation of deconstruction of familiar mathematical entities, most notably clear when it comes to N N .

arxiv-2312-00701.title: Rigidity results for large displacement quotients of mapping class groups
arxiv-2312-00701.creator: Giorgio Mangioni
arxiv-2312-00701.description: Abstract . We consider quotients of mapping class groups of orientable, finite type surfaces by subgroups whose action on the curve graph has large displacement. This class includes quotients by the normal closure of a pseudo-Anosov element, the mapping class group itself, and in view of forthcoming work of Abbott-Berlyne-Ng-Rasmussen also random quotients.

arxiv-2405-16976.title: Generalized hydrodynamics and approach to Generalized Gibbs equilibrium for a classical harmonic chain
arxiv-2405-16976.creator: Saurav Pandey 1, Abhishek Dhar 1 and Anupam Kundu 1
arxiv-2405-16976.description: Abstract We study the evolution of a classical harmonic chain with nearest-neighbor interactions starting from domain wall initial conditions. The initial state is taken to be either a product of two Gibbs Ensembles (GEs) with unequal temperatures on the two halves of the chain or a product of two Generalized Gibbs Ensembles (GGEs) with different parameters in the two halves.

arxiv-2502-13537.title: Precise quantile function estimation from the characteristic function
arxiv-2502-13537.creator: Gero Junike
arxiv-2502-13537.description: Abstract We provide theoretical error bounds for the accurate numerical computation of the quantile function given the characteristic function of a continuous random variable. We show theoretically and empirically that the numerical error of the quantile function is typically several orders of magnitude larger than the numerical error of the cumulative distribution function for probabilities close to zero or one.

arxiv-2505-23803.title: MultiPhishGuard: An LLM-based Multi-Agent System for Phishing Email Detection DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: the 2025 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security; October 13–17, 2025; Taipei, Taiwan ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/2018/06 CCS: Security and privacy CCS: Computing methodol
arxiv-2505-23803.creator: Yinuo Xue, Eric Spero, Yun Sing Koh, Giovanni Russello
arxiv-2505-23803.description: Abstract . Phishing email detection faces critical challenges from evolving adversarial tactics and heterogeneous attack patterns. Traditional detection methods, such as rule-based filters and denylists, often struggle to keep pace with these evolving tactics, leading to false negatives and compromised security. While machine learning approaches have improved detection accuracy, they still face challenges adapting to novel phishing strategies.

pmc-10553083.title: Gender-based differences in the job titles and lifestyles in the cataract and refractive surgery society in Japan
pmc-10553083.creator: Naoko Kato, Takashi Kojima, Masayuki Ouchi, Tomoaki Nakamura, Yoshihiro Tokuda, Tadayuki Yakushiji, Kazuo Ichikawa
pmc-10553083.description: To investigate sex differences in the titles and lifestyles of Japanese ophthalmologists, we evaluated work places and private lives. Retrospective cross-sectional study. The study included 1721 members (1344 males and 377 females) of the Japanese Society of Cataract and Refractive Surgery. An online, anonymized questionnaire was distributed to the society members.

pmc-10632670.title: CPT1A mediates chemoresistance in human hypopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma via ATG16L1-dependent cellular autophagy
pmc-10632670.creator: Lianhui Sun, Xing Wang, Lixiao Chen, Zheng Gao, Songhui Xu, Chen Hu, Guangjian Fan, Baoxin Wang, Tingting Feng, Wang Wang, Xinjiang Ying
pmc-10632670.description: Hypopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (HSCC) is a highly aggressive malignancy that constitutes approximately 95% of all hypopharyngeal carcinomas, and it carries a poor prognosis. The primary factor influencing the efficacy of anti-cancer drugs for this type of carcinoma is chemoresistance. Carnitine palmitoyltransferase 1A (CPT1A) has been associated with tumor progression in various cancers, including breast, gastric, lung, and prostate cancer.

pmc-10751502.title: Characteristics of adverse drug reactions due to nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs: a cross-sectional study
pmc-10751502.creator: Cholticha Sonsupap, Pattreya Pokhakul, Tetsuyoshi Kariya, Yunosuke Suzuki, Nobuyuki Hamajima, Eiko Yamamoto
pmc-10751502.description: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) are widely used for treating pain and inflammation. Spontaneous adverse drug reaction (ADR) reports represent a rich data source for the detection of unknown and rare ADRs. This cross-sectional study aimed to analyze the characteristics of ADRs due to NSAIDs in Thailand.

pmc-11634673.title: Transient negativity for the anti-TIF1γ antibody before treatment in juvenile dermatomyositis
pmc-11634673.creator: Yuji Fujita, Takashi Matsushita, Megumi Sato, Shigemi Yoshihara
pmc-11634673.description: nsiently tested negative for the anti-TIF1γ antibody prior to treatment. The patient was a 7-year-old girl with a skin rash accompanied by itching who was being treated for atopic dermatitis (AD). She subsequently developed thigh and joint pain, resulting in a visit to our hospital.

pmc-12563059.title: Psychometric Properties of the Violence Exposure Scale in Ecuadorian Adolescents and Its Relationship with Child-to-Parent Violence
pmc-12563059.creator: Paola Bustos-Benítez, Andrés Ramírez, Javier Herrero Díez, M Carmen Cano-Lozano, Stephen Houghton

pmc-12613581.title: Reengineering glycyrrhetinic acid into a therapeutic oligomer for targeted tumor therapy with cardioprotection
pmc-12613581.creator: Zixin Wang, Bo Su, Alu Ouyang, ZiXuan Liang, Pingyun Yuan, Xin Qin, Yu Li, Xuejing Huang, Ling Fan, Hongwei Guo, Ronghua Jin
pmc-12613581.description: To overcome the inherent limitations of conventional nanocarriers such as therapeutic inefficacy and suboptimal drug loading capacity, a novel “polymeric nanodrug” strategy was developed. This approach redefines nanodrug design by employing glycyrrhetinic acid (GA) simultaneously as a bioactive agent and a polymerizable targeting monomer to synthesize poly-glycyrrhetinic acid (PGA), achieving near-theoretical drug loading approaching 100%.

pmc-12644804.title: A reduced sensor-based efficient and robust MPPT nonlinear controller for grid-integrated photovoltaic energy systems operating under rapidly changing climatic conditions
pmc-12644804.creator: Abdulaziz Almalaq, Andres Annuk, Tao Jin, Mohamed A Mohamed
pmc-12644804.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This paper proposes a reduced sensor-based nonlinear maximum power point tracking (MPPT) controller for grid-integrated photovoltaic (PV) systems operating under rapidly changing climatic conditions. Unlike conventional approaches that require costly irradiance sensors, the proposed method employs a mathematical irradiance estimation model and a radial basis function neural network to generate optimal reference voltages, which are then enforced by a backstepping nonlinear controller. This two-stage design enables fast and robust MPPT while maintaining DC-link stability and grid power quality.

pmc-13336599.title: Al─N Co‐Doped LLZO Solid Electrolytes via One‐Step Sintering: Toward High Ionic Conductivity
pmc-13336599.creator: Hao Zhang, Yaocong Wang, Quande Che, Jiaming Wu, Yanzhu Zhang, Dongxu Mao, Xundao Liu, Jiajie Li, Zhengmao Ye, Dehua Dong
pmc-13336599.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Garnet‐type Li7La3Zr2O12 (LLZO) is a promising solid electrolyte for solid‐state lithium batteries owing to its relatively high ionic conductivity and wide electrochemical window. However, its conductivity still needs further improvement to meet practical application requirements. Herein, we propose for the first time a cation–anion co‐doping strategy to synthesize Al─N co‐doped LLZO via a one‐step sintering process, achieving a high ionic conductivity of 2.19 × 10−3 S cm−1.

pmc-13503139.title: PARP inhibition attenuates neuroinflammation and demyelination in a rat model of multiple sclerosis: A longitudinal [11C]PBR28 TSPO PET imaging study
pmc-13503139.creator: Ge Li, Inês F. Antunes, Zihe Ming, Chunhui Wu, Bart Cornelissen, Erik FJ. de Vries
pmc-13503139.description: Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) plays important role in DNA repair, but is also involved in other cellular processes. PARP inhibition was suggested to suppress inflammatory signaling and has been proposed as potential treatment for neuroinflammatory disorders like multiple sclerosis. Yet, its effects on lesion-associated neuroinflammation in vivo remain insufficiently understood.

pmc-13546280.title: Glycemic Patterns Assessed by Continuous Glucose Monitoring in People with Type 2 Diabetes Treated with Insulin Glargine 100 U/mL in Primary Care: The GPDetect Study
pmc-13546280.creator: Virginia Bellido, Ana Cebrián, Cristóbal Morales, Alberto S de las Hazas, Alfonso Soto-Gonzalez, Carla Morer-Liñan, José M Borrachero, Gabriel Cuatrecases, Elena L García, Judith López-Fernández, Silvia Lozano-García, Álvaro M Bayón, Cristina M Niño-Azcarate, Oscar Laclaustra, Paulina Fuentealba
pmc-13546280.description: IntroductionHypoglycemia is a common complication in people with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) treated with basal insulin, yet its true prevalence in real-world primary care remains underexplored. This study used blinded continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) to assess glycemic patterns in patients with T2DM on basal insulin-supported oral therapy (BOT) with insulin glargine 100 U/mL (Gla-100) in Spain.
